transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-02-14
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Turner (Redwood AE), Evan Li (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (GreenWave Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (GreenWave Platform), Sara Kim (GreenWave Data Privacy)

Summary (auto): Drafted pilot SLOs and measurement plan; decided on two-step approach (TPOT stress runs + TTFT latency-critical runs), agreed on data artifacts to exchange.

[00:00] Maya Turner: alright everyone thanks for joining, is this time still good? we've got about 75 minutes on the calendar so high level we want to run through success criteria, what your workloads look like, and propose a bench plan, cool?
[00:27] Priya Singh: yeah sounds good, uh thanks maya. Quick note, we're under a hiring freeze so the pilot needs to be lightweight and show delta on latency/cost quickly, okay?
[00:45] Evan Li: understood. before we dive, can you confirm the two primary workload shapes? you had chat sessions with ~1-2k token context and high qps for short completions, and a smaller set of long generations for summarization? is that right?
[01:12] Tom Alvarez: yeah that's the gist. Most calls are chatty — few-turn, each turn ~100-300 tokens. But we have a nightly summarization job that can be 2-3k tokens and runs in bursts.
[01:35] Sara Kim: from privacy we need proof of no logs retention, and that we can route traffic through our VPC; we may also need KMS integrated in the pilot if possible.
[01:55] Maya Turner: totally. For the pilot SLOs we typically recommend a two-track: TTFT (time to first token) for latency-sensitive chat use-cases and TPOT (tokens per second sustained) for throughput/batch jobs. We usually measure p95 and p99 for TTFT and p50 for TPOT but we can adapt.
[02:22] Priya Singh: ok what are realistic p95/p99 numbers? i.e., we'd like to set something measurable for our SLAs.
[02:35] Evan Li: based on similar customers, for small chat completions (up to 512 tokens context+response) p95 TTFT target we see ~120-200ms on dedicated GPU pools, p99 ~400-600ms. Public hosted with multi-tenant can be a bit higher. For TPOT, we specify sustained tokens/sec per GPU — e.g., 600-1200 tokens/sec on A100-class inference config depending on quantization.
[03:05] Tom Alvarez: those p99 numbers feel low, are they measured with KV cache primed? our traffic has a lot of repetition so priming could change numbers.
[03:22] Evan Li: good call — priming matters. For TTFT we measure cold vs warm cache; pilot will need both: a cold-start scenario (unprimed KV) and an expected production steady-state where prefix caching reduces token compute. We'll include cache-priming runs in the plan.
[03:45] Priya Singh: We care about tail latencies during peak (30 minute burst windows). Our SLO needs to be p99 under peak load no lower than 1s — we can stretch to 1.5s as a fall-back if cost savings are significant.
[04:05] Maya Turner: noted. For acceptance criteria let's draft: chat p95 under 250ms, p99 under 1s for 95% of peak windows; batch summarization TPOT target of X tokens/sec across N GPUs — we'll quantify once we have token mix. Does that sound reasonable as a starting point?
[04:33] Priya Singh: yes that's reasonable, though we need explicit cost per 1M tokens estimates as well.
[04:45] Evan Li: we'll include cost modeling — Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles. For the pilot we'll run 1) TPOT stress test to find throughput ceiling and degradation curve, and 2) TTFT randomized load with production-shaped rdps to capture p95/p99.
[05:10] Tom Alvarez: how do you shape traffic? do you replay raw traces or synthesize user arrival processes?
[05:22] Evan Li: we prefer replaying time-series traces when available — preserves burstiness — but also supplement with synthetic poisson plus bursts to stress tails. For token mixes we'll apply sampled token lengths from your export.
[05:40] Priya Singh: we can export 48 hours of anonymized traces — we'll scrub user ids. how should we deliver them?
[05:50] Maya Turner: secure link to the Redwood pilot bucket works; we'll provide instructions. sara, on privacy do you have concerns with the bucket approach?
[06:05] Sara Kim: fine if it's a customer-controlled S3 with cross-account role, or a signed tarball. KMS key usage needs to be visible — we may request an attestation.
[06:20] Evan Li: we can do cross-account role and accept an encrypted tarball. we'll include a minimal privacy checklist in the pilot SOW.
[06:35] Priya Singh: ok timeline — how long for the TPOT runs and the TTFT runs?
[06:45] Evan Li: TPOT ceiling runs typically take 2-4 hours per configuration (varying batch sizes / quant), TTFT latency runs we run several 30-minute windows across peak/off-peak, total ~4-6 hours including priming and steady-state validation. So total execution time per pilot iteration ~1 day but we'll plan for a 2-day window to collect robust tails.
[07:12] Tom Alvarez: what about instrumentation? we need token-level cost breakdowns.
[07:20] Maya Turner: Redwood Console will provide token-level latency and cost breakdown per route/model. We'll attach the console export and raw logs to the pilot report.
[07:35] Priya Singh: and how do you measure TTFT exactly? first byte vs first semantic token — different tooling can vary.
[07:48] Evan Li: good question. we record Time To First Byte from the gateway and also compute Time To First Token at the runtime level when available; we correlate both. For consistency we'll align on gateway TTFT metric for your SLO but include runtime TTFT in the report.
[08:10] Priya Singh: ok. Competitive question: we evaluate Bedrock and Anthropic — how will Redwood compare in the pilot?
[08:24] Maya Turner: we'll surface relative latency/cost on identical traces and model choices. we won't run competitors directly (customer may), but we can help design a fair comparison; we also include quantization options and dedicated vs shared baselines.
[08:40] Sara Kim: legal side — do you have SOC2 type II in place? we need that for procurement.
[08:50] Maya Turner: yes SOC 2 Type II in progress; we can share compliance docs via our secure portal as part of the SOW.
[09:00] Priya Singh: acceptance criteria recap please.
[09:05] Evan Li: acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) Chat TTFT p95 < 250ms and p99 < 1s under production-shaped peak for primary route; 2) Batch TPOT achieves at least 80% of our modeled tokens/sec projection on dedicated pool; 3) No data retention beyond agreed retention window; 4) Compatibility with cross-account encrypted trace delivery.
[09:37] Priya Singh: ok fine. action items?
[09:40] Maya Turner: i'll send the benchmark matrix and draft SOW with the measurement plan and sample traffic profile by Wednesday (2026-02-18). Evan will build the TPOT harness and synthetic burst scripts and share them by Friday (2026-02-20). Tom will export the 48h anonymized traces by Tuesday (2026-02-17). Sara will confirm KMS constraints by EOD 2026-02-16.
[10:05] Tom Alvarez: quick detail — can you surface the GPU type you'd use in Dedicated? we may want A10G vs A100 comparisons.
[10:15] Evan Li: yes we can include both. quantization will change throughput numbers significantly — e.g., dynamic 4-bit gives 2-4x throughput on A100.
[10:30] Priya Singh: also let's capture warmup costs — initial priming run tokens should be counted in pilot cost estimate.
[10:40] Maya Turner: noted; we'll include a cost annex explaining priming overhead and amortization. we'll also include a recommended autoscaling policy for your peak windows.
[10:55] Sara Kim: any red flags on security for the pilot?
[11:00] Evan Li: no immediate red flags; cross-account S3 plus KMS is standard. if you need air-gapped we'll scope private deployment but that's out of campaign pilot budget.
[11:15] Priya Singh: final timeline check — can we do the pilot run week of Feb 24?
[11:20] Maya Turner: yes that aligns with our infra calendar. let's pencil Feb 25-26 for the execution window.
[11:30] Priya Singh: perfect. thanks everyone.
[11:33] Maya Turner: thanks — recap in the notes and we'll follow up with SOW + matrix.

Closing notes: referenced artifacts — pilot benchmark matrix (link: https://redwood.in/benchmarks/greenwave-pilot), sample SOW draft (link), and traffic export template.

End of transcript.
